key_insight: The paper shows that zero-shot active feature acquisition can be done by eliciting only the LLM’s trustworthy unary and pairwise feature statistics, then using a maximum-entropy closure to guide sequential feature selection.
clinical_relevance: This could help support decision-making in heterogeneous clinical cases, such as IBD, by reducing the number of features needed before making a classification or ranking decision.
method: Ask the LLM for sufficient statistics, not full sequential plans
Use a maximum-entropy MRF closure to resolve discriminative-statistics ambiguity
Apply the framework to binary classification and top-k identification
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on an Inflammatory Bowel Disease cohort and, according to the abstract, outperformed the LLM on both real labels and extracted beliefs, with especially strong gains on the hardest patients.
watch_item: Performance depends on the LLM reliably providing only discriminative statistics, so the approach may be sensitive to elicitation quality and may need careful validation before clinical use.
paper_title: Zero-Shot Active Feature Acquisition via LLM-Elicitation
